layout.boundary: soft organic transition; no hard modern UI divider
layout.safe_margin: generous; all text must remain comfortably inside canvas

left_panel.texture: subtle parchment, stone, or woven-paper texture; never noisy
left_panel.dividers: thin restrained ornamental rules may be used

typography.optional_subcopy: one short line only when useful

right_scene.historical_world: ancient Near East appropriate to Genesis
right_scene.purpose: visualize only what the current aliyah can responsibly support
right_scene.composition: narrative scene with depth, natural light, restrained drama
right_scene.historical_fidelity: prefer plausible Bronze Age / ancient Near Eastern materials, clothing, landscape and architecture without false precision
forbid: crosses, churches, halos or unrelated later religious symbols
people, events or symbols absent from or unsupported by the current passage

photographic_direction.scope: Right-side scene only. Keep the left information panel and every required character crisp and fully legible; do not apply optical blur or light bloom to text. Preserve the existing unified 1200x630 cover layout.
photographic_direction.intent: Plan the viewpoint, framing, focus and light like a professional environmental photographer while retaining warm painterly realism and the current parasha's visual identity.
photographic_direction.narrative_focus: From the current RUN's passage and theme, first identify the main person, relationship, expression, gesture, object or landscape and the meaningful instant to depict. Direct the viewer's eye toward that focus.
photographic_direction.viewpoint_and_framing: Choose the viewpoint for the current passage's central action, relationship or tension. Do not default to a frontal, evenly weighted tableau. Consider oblique or over-the-shoulder views for dialogue, close views for meaningful hands/actions, and wider views for communal movement. Use frontal symmetry deliberately when it serves the theme; do not fix every scene at 45 degrees or at a low angle.
photographic_direction.depth_of_field: When suitable, build foreground, main-subject and background depth: a softly defocused near element, a sharply readable main subject, and a gently defocused distant setting. Let focus and blur change plausibly with distance from the focal plane; avoid uniform blur, cutout halos or arbitrarily blurred body parts. Do not invent people or props merely to create a foreground layer.
photographic_direction.relational_focus: If a relationship or group is the subject, keep the relevant faces, hands and actions readable together through staging and sufficient depth of field. Do not isolate one face so strongly that the passage's central relationship disappears.
photographic_direction.lens_and_aperture: Select the lens character and depth of field for each scene. Intimate portraits may use a shallower depth of field; communal or landscape scenes may use a deeper one. Focal-length and f-number descriptions are optional visual guidance, never fixed numeric requirements. Strong bokeh and three distinct layers are not mandatory in every scene.
photographic_direction.lighting_and_texture: Use a coherent light direction, soft modeled shadows and, when appropriate, restrained rim or reflected light to reveal faces, cloth and spatial depth. Retain natural skin and material texture without plastic smoothing, excessive HDR or oversharpening.
photographic_direction.variation: Choose composition and lighting afresh from the current passage. Do not mechanically repeat golden sunsets, upward-looking posed groups, the same focal subject, camera angle or foreground object.
photographic_direction.fidelity_and_continuity: Current passage fidelity and exact required text take precedence over photographic effects. Preserve the parasha palette, materials and historical-world continuity; do not add unsupported actions, relationships or events or use past images or generation identifiers.
photographic_direction.viewer_position: Before selecting an angle, decide where the viewer stands within the story: a participant at the table, a listener to a conversation, an observer of departure, or another position supported by the passage. Use that role to choose camera height, distance and direction.
photographic_direction.visual_path: Design angle and depth of field together: use existing table edges, gestures, gazes or terrain to lead attention through the scene toward the main action. Describe the viewer's role, concrete camera position, meaningful instant and intended visual path in the ephemeral CURRENT RUN IMAGE PACKAGE. Do not substitute tilted horizons or wide-angle distortion for a meaningful viewpoint, or add unsupported props.

parasha_profile_policy.lookup: exact Japanese parasha name only; never guess slug
parasha_profile_policy.if_missing: ChatGPT creates one new profile before image generation, writes it to ver3/config/parasha-image/<slug>.json, and adds the exact Japanese parasha name to index.json
new_profile_basis: the current parasha identity and its broad biblical world
parasha_profile_policy.existing_profile_update: do not overwrite automatically during a production run; use the existing profile unless the user explicitly requests a design revision

checks: theme is derived from current passage
optional subcopy is consistent with current callout2
right-side scene is consistent with current passage
right-side visual focus and viewpoint support the current passage and theme
focus and blur vary plausibly with scene depth when appropriate; strong bokeh is not required

theme and required text remain clear at thumbnail viewing size
the viewer's position and selected camera angle are visibly realized and convey the current passage's central action or tension
